official.deadline_note: Deadline is 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET with no extension; once submitted, applications cannot be changed. Decisions notified mid-February 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2026 call (Application Guidance dated 9 June 2026; the visit must fall between 1 March 2027 and 29 February 2028)
official.status_note: The ERS VISIT grant page displays 'CALL OPEN' and states 'Applications for the ERS VISIT Grant are open'; the call opened 13 July 2026 and the fellowship portfolio page lists the VISIT grant status as 'Open' with next deadline 31 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The guidance enumerates only a travel allowance and an accommodation/meals allowance and states that no additional costs will be considered; tuition is not a funded cost of this grant.
benefits: Travel allowance of EUR 600 for mobility between European countries (including both EU and non-EU states)
EUR 2,000 for mobility from Europe to non-Europe, or non-Europe to Europe (long distance flight)
Accommodation / meals allowance of EUR 200 (fixed amount per day of stay and travel)
Grant calculated on a fixed basis for each awardee regardless of the type of accommodation or real costs of life and travel; no expense receipts will be requested
Paid in two instalments: 60% of the travel grant ahead of the visit and the second instalment (40%) after the end of the visit based on the actual number of days of stay
eligibility: Clinicians and researchers must hold a postgraduate degree such as PhD, MD(Res) or equivalent; allied healthcare professionals must hold a minimum of an MSc, or equivalent degree, at the time of application (e.g. BSc degree with evidence of continuous specialised training in respiratory health)
Applicants must be ERS active members for at least one year when applying

Open to applicants within 5 years of appointment to clinical or academic equivalent of Associate Professor / Reader level, taking career breaks into account; applicants holding a professor title are not eligible

Applicants must not have worked at the host institution or lived in the host country in the 12 months prior to the application deadline; exchanges between two institutions within the same country are not allowed
Applicants must have adequate fluency in a language that permits effective communication at the host institution
All nationalities, European and non-European based applicants may submit a proposal; return to the home institution after the visit is mandatory
requirements: The applicant should be invited by the host institution to give a lecture/seminar or lead a similar knowledge exchange event during the stay
The visit should last a minimum of one week and must not exceed one month

The visit plan is the most important component of the application and should be prepared by the applicant with the contribution of the host institution, detailed, clear and realistic with a scope achievable within the set time frame
Applicants must identify and contact the host institution themselves; ERS will not provide any assistance in the search of a host institution
The ERS VISIT grant cannot run concurrently with other similar funding schemes received during the same period, even those funded by other agencies
documents: VISIT Grant Application Guidance 2026 (published reference document)
Host Institution Invitation Form, completed and signed by the host supervisor
Home Supervisor Support Form, completed and signed
Scanned copy of the applicant's ID card or passport
Letter from the applicant's institution stating their position and confirming leave and return, plus a CV including major publications (maximum 2 pages)
selection_criteria: Planned activities (30%): relevance of the visit to the respiratory area; feasibility and quality of the work plan; competence and expertise of the host institution in relation to the applicant; opportunity to build collaboration and networking
Quality and potential of applicant (30%): quality of CV (qualifications, experience, previous background); potential of the applicant to achieve clinical expertise or research independence

Post visit activities and potential impact (40%): potential impact on the applicant's career and added value for the home institution and at country level; potential of the visit to lead to new international collaborations; quality of plans for knowledge exchange on return

Selection made by the ERS College of Experts through peer review with scoring, a ranking teleconference, ERS Science Council decision and final endorsement by the ERS Executive Committee; the choice of host institution is itself assessed and applications without appropriate justification will not be considered
coverage: Travel allowance for mobility between the home and host countries: EUR 600 between European countries, EUR 2,000 for long-distance mobility between Europe and non-Europe
Accommodation / meals allowance of EUR 200 per day, calculated for the full duration of the stay from the day of travel to the day of departure
No travel support for partners or family members (spouse, children, etc.)
The grant does not cover undergraduate studies and is not designed solely to cover the costs of attending workshops, courses, conferences or congresses
application_method: Email the completed application form with all supporting documents to scientific@ersnet.org by 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET; incomplete applications will not be considered and no changes are accepted once submitted
official.application_route: Download the ERS VISIT Application Form 2026, complete the visit plan, attach the signed Host Institution Invitation Form and Home Supervisor Support Form, the institutional letter, the ID/passport scan and a 2-page CV, and email the complete package to scientific@ersnet.org by 31 October 2026 (23:59 CET).
official.citizenship_residency: All nationalities, European and non-European based applicants may submit a proposal; no citizenship or residency restriction is published.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - explicitly open to applicants of all nationalities, European and non-European, with mobility supported from Europe to Europe, from Europe to non-Europe, and from non-Europe to Europe.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must work in the field of respiratory health/medicine and be actively engaged in respiratory health research, practice and advocacy; applicants must be ERS active members for at least one year when applying.
official.duration: From one week up to a maximum of one month; the visit can start from 1 March 2027 and recipients have 12 months from this date to conduct the visit (the host form states the visit must fall between 1 March 2027 and 29 February 2028).
official.description: The ERS VISIT grant, funded by the European Respiratory Society, is designed to support mid-career investigators, clinicians and allied healthcare professionals who are transitioning to more established stages of their careers, facilitating visits between laboratories, hospitals, university departments, research centres, clinical centres and not-for-profit organisations to foster collaboration and continued professional growth in the field of respiratory health. The programme is not for clinical training or research projects, which are covered by the ERS fellowship programmes instead.
official.region: Europe (ERS is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland); open to applicants and host institutions worldwide, with mobility supported between Europe and non-Europe
official.program_type: Professional society international visit/travel grant for mid-career professionals
official.english_requirement: No IELTS/TOEFL score is published. The published rule is that applicants must have adequate fluency in a language that permits effective communication at the host institution, certified by the host supervisor in the Host Institution Invitation Form.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fixed-rate travel grant rather than a salary: ERS pays EUR 200 per day for accommodation and meals plus a travel allowance of EUR 600 (within Europe) or EUR 2,000 (long-distance), disbursed 60% before the visit and 40% afterwards with no receipts required. Reviewers weight post-visit impact at 40% and planned activities at 30%, so the case you must make is what a one-week-to-one-month visit changes for your home institution and which collaborations it locks in. Everything hinges on a host you arrange yourself - ERS states plainly that it gives no help finding one - and you must already have been an active ERS member for at least a year by the deadline. Note the 40% instalment is paid pro-rata on actual days of stay after your visit report, so shorten the trip and the money shrinks with it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career respiratory clinicians, scientists and allied health professionals with a PhD/MD(Resp)/MSc who can secure a host abroad on their own and need modest bridge funding for a short collaboration or networking visit.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your ERS membership has been active for at least one year by 31 October 2026 - this is an eligibility bar, not a formality.
Confirm you are within 5 years of appointment to Associate Professor/Reader level (career breaks deducted) and hold no professor title.
Line up a host supervisor early: they must co-develop the visit plan, commit to a lecture or knowledge-exchange event, and sign the Host Institution Invitation Form.
Obtain the Home Supervisor Support Form and a letter from your institution confirming your position, your leave and your guaranteed return.
Draft a realistic one-week-to-one-month visit plan with a day-level timeline and an explicit knowledge-transfer plan for your home institution.
Prepare a scan of your ID/passport and a 2-page CV with your major publications.
Email the full package to scientific@ersnet.org ahead of 31 October 2026, 23:59 CET - there are no extensions and no edits after submission.
common_rejection_risks: A weak or unrealistic visit plan - it carries 30% of the score and the choice of host is itself a scored criterion; the guidance warns that applications without appropriate host justification will not be considered.
Missing or unsigned supervisor forms: applicants without complete host invitation forms by the deadline are declared ineligible.
Applying while already working at the host institution or living in the host country within the last 12 months.
Pitching a clinical training or research project - ERS explicitly redirects those uses to its fellowship programmes.
Neglecting the post-visit section: generic career statements squander the single largest scoring block (40%).
Funding overlap: holding any concurrent stipend, salary or grant that covers living and mobility costs disqualifies the application.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa fees and any administrative travel formalities, comprehensive travel insurance including medical and accident cover (explicitly the recipient's responsibility), any taxes arising in the home or host country, travel for a partner or family (explicitly not funded), and anything beyond the fixed allowances - the guidance states no additional costs will be considered.
document_audit: The application form, host invitation and home supervisor forms must state identical details; the guidance says discrepancies make the definitive source ambiguous, and host forms with mismatches sink the file.
The host supervisor's signature must be handwritten or certificate-based - typed sign-offs are not accepted.
The CV is capped at 2 pages including major publications; over-length documents are cut to fit the requirement.
ID/passport scans are used only by the ERS office to check eligibility and are not shown to reviewers, but their absence blocks the application.
Each additional host institution needs its own completed invitation letter - plan for two signatures if the visit spans two sites.

The guidance in places references an 'online application platform' while the deadline and the 2026 form specify email submission to scientific@ersnet.org; confirm the operative route with the ERS office before the deadline week.
alerts: Timing squeeze: the call ran 13 July to 31 October 2026 - roughly 15 weeks to secure a host abroad, so host outreach has to start the week the call opens.
The grant cannot run concurrently with any other stipend, salary or grant covering living and mobility allowances, even from other agencies.
The visit must start on or after 1 March 2027 and be completed within 12 months; if it does not happen within a year, funds already transferred must be returned and the grant is cancelled.
Only actual days of stay are funded - cutting a visit short reduces the final instalment pro-rata, and delaying the start by more than 3 months risks revocation.
ERS accepts no liability for health, safety, insurance or taxes, and recipients are neither agents nor employees of ERS.
Decisions are final and appeals are not considered unless ERS made a mistake; reviewer scores are never disclosed.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The applicant emails the complete package (Word application form, visit plan, both signed supervisor forms, institutional letter, ID/passport scan, 2-page CV) to scientific@ersnet.org; ERS College of Experts members score and shortlist, a teleconference ranks the round, the Science Council selects and the Executive Committee endorses, and outcomes are notified in mid-February 2027.
